name: Semantic Transaction Isolation for Cognitive State
research_question: Can authoritative FRANK/Clay multi-field state remain replay-safe under concurrent learning, correction, rollback and effect paths using only per-field atomics, or is snapshot/transaction isolation required at invariant boundaries?

hypotheses.claim: Authoritative multi-field cognitive state that participates in one invariant must be observed/committed through a snapshot-consistent or equivalent serializable boundary; per-field atomics alone admit fractured states.
hypotheses.falsifier: Show an implementation using only per-field atomic operations that preserves the same cross-field invariants and deterministic replay under exhaustive concurrency schedules without global serialization.

hypotheses.claim: The current ClayCode language likely does not require a new transaction syntax primitive; a typed runtime/ABI/stdlib transaction contract may satisfy the need while preserving the less-change-more-compile rule.
evidence: current ClayCode acceptance contract already requires concurrency/atomics, FFI, capability/effect gateway and DB service execution
hypotheses.falsifier: Produce a real ClayCode/FRANK program that cannot express or safely lower the required transaction semantics through existing semantic/effect primitives plus typed runtime ABI.

hypotheses.claim: Consequential effect commits should bind to a state transaction/snapshot receipt so an effect cannot commit against stale authoritative state after concurrent cognitive-state mutation.
evidence: EXP-STI-02 lost-update mechanism + Harness effect/outcome/re-entry authority boundary
hypotheses.falsifier: Demonstrate a target harness protocol that prevents all stale-state effect commits under concurrency without binding commit to an equivalent state version/read-set guard.

counterhypotheses.claim: A single-threaded deterministic scheduler around all authoritative cognitive state can eliminate the need for transaction isolation.
counterhypotheses.next_test: Benchmark semantic correctness and latency/throughput against snapshot transactions on H1/H2 workloads.

counterhypotheses.claim: Actor-style ownership/partitioning can make most state updates conflict-free, requiring transactions only for small invariant groups.
counterhypotheses.next_test: Classify FRANK state by ownership and enumerate cross-owner invariants.

counterhypotheses.claim: Derived non-authoritative state such as caches/activation can remain eventually consistent if epoch-tagged and excluded from authority decisions.
counterhypotheses.next_test: Lesion delayed derived-state refresh and verify authoritative outcomes/replay remain invariant.

experiments.method: Exhaustively enumerate all 20 order-preserving interleavings of a 3-step writer upgrading prototype_version, calibration_version and active_version from 5 to 6 and a 3-step reader observing the same fields.
experiments.interpretation: Per-field atomicity does not imply invariant-level snapshot consistency.

experiments.method: Exhaustively enumerate all 6 order-preserving interleavings of two read-then-write transactions on one versioned object. Compare naive last-write-wins with compare-and-swap commit guard.
experiments.interpretation: Version-guarded commit converts overlapping stale writes into explicit conflicts rather than silent lineage loss.

external_evidence.source: Berenson et al., A Critique of ANSI SQL Isolation Levels, MSR-TR-95-51 (1995)
external_evidence.relevance: Defines snapshot isolation and documents that weaker isolation descriptions miss important anomalies.
Serializable isolation aims to make committed concurrent executions equivalent to some serial order and surfaces serialization failures requiring retry.

cross_connections.delta: Add transaction/snapshot receipt requirements to CC-WP-07 runtime ABI/FFI and CC-WP-09 concurrency-memory tests; do not add new language syntax unless an executable counterexample proves runtime/stdlib lowering insufficient.

Prioritize invariant-group transaction/effect atomicity, exact snapshots, conflict receipts and replay under concurrent updates; distinguish authoritative transactional state from epoch-tagged rebuildable derivatives.
Add exhaustive/minimized race tests for fractured snapshots, lost updates, stale snapshot effect commit, retry/serialization failure, crash between state commit and effect/outcome/re-entry.

negative_results.statement: Per-field atomics alone are insufficient for the tested three-field invariant: exactly half of legal reader/writer interleavings produced a state tuple impossible as a single committed version.
Naive last-write-wins on versioned concurrent read-modify-write is not lineage-safe: 4/6 legal interleavings silently lose one update.

implementation_recommendation.authority_rule: Transaction expressibility does not grant effect authority; external effects still require the existing capability/commit gateway.
